3188.t: Compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀯𐀹𐀊 (a-si-wi-ja). There is no current consensus on the origin of the word.

3167.t: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew אָמֵן (āmḗn, “so be it”, “surely”).

3144.t: As this word is also Doric and Aeolic, the connection with ἵστημι (hĭ́stēmĭ, “to stand”) must be given up.

3160.t: Uncertain. Could be from a Proto-Indo-European *bʰes- (“to blow”), with cognates including Sanskrit भस्त्रा॑ (bhástrā, “bellows”), अप्सु॑ (ápsu, “without breath”), and Albanian badër.

3134.t: From a Proto-Indo-European *puH-ro-s (“corn, wheat”), also reflected in Lithuanian pū́ras (“single winter corn”), Proto-Slavic *py̑rь (“dog-grass”), and Old English fyrs (idem).

3135.t: Borrowed from a foreign eastern language. Compare various Indo-Iranian terms like Sogdian 𐼾𐼴𐽀𐼹𐼻𐼸 (pwrδnk), Bactrian πορλαγγο-ζινο (porlango-zino), Pashto پړانګ (pṛāng), Persian پلنگ (palang), and Sanskrit पृदाकु (pṛ́dāku).

3107.t: From Proto-Hellenic *mū́s, from Proto-Indo-European *múHs (“mouse”). Cognates include Latin mūs, Sanskrit मूष् (mū́ṣ), Old Armenian մուկն (mukn) and Old English mūs (English mouse).

3199.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *h₁én Ancient Greek ἐν (en) Ancient Greek ἐν- (en-) Proto-Indo-European *werǵ- Proto-Indo-European *-om Proto-Indo-European *wérǵom Proto-Hellenic *wérgon Ancient Greek ἔργον (érgon) Proto-Indo-European *-os…

3143.t: The etymology remains highly uncertain, but Beekes suspects a Pre-Greek origin.

3147.t: From συμπαθής (sumpathḗs, “affected by like feelings; exerting mutual influence, interacting”) + -ια (-ia).

3128.t: Etymology tree Ancient Greek προ- (pro-) Ancient Greek ἵστημι (hístēmi) Ancient Greek προΐστημι (proḯstēmi) Proto-Indo-European *-tósder.

3136.t: From earlier *πάκσνα (*páksnā), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂ǵ-, like πήγνυμι (pḗgnumi, “I fasten”).

3153.t: Since long, connected with Latin fīcus and Old Armenian թուզ (tʻuz), and considered a borrowing from a Mediterranean (Pre-Greek) or Anatolian substrate source, from which Hebrew שִׁקְמָה (šiqmā́, “sycamore fig”) – borrowed into συκάμινος (sukáminos) – and…

3174.t: From ἀξιόω (axióō, “to think or deem worthy”) + -μα (-ma).

3176.t: From ἀπο- (ăpo-, “from”) + δείκνυμι (deíknūmĭ, “to point out, show”).

3106.t: Unknown. The long vowel makes it unlikely to be from the same root as μανία (mănĭ́ā).

3164.t: A double-ablauted formation from κέλευθος (kéleuthos, “path”) + copulative ἀ- (a-).

3100.t: From Proto-Indo-European *mel- (“strong, better”). Cognates include Latin melius, multus and Latvian milns.

3154.t: From Proto-Hellenic *trís, from Proto-Indo-European *trís; related to τρεῖς (treîs, “three”). Cognates include Sanskrit त्रिस् (trís) and Latin ter.

3148.t: Often connected with σφεδανός (sphedanós), σφοδρός (sphodrós), σφαδᾴζω (sphadāízō), and Sanskrit स्पन्दते (spandate, “to vibrate, tremble, quake”), as well as with Latin funda (“sling”), with formation structure similar to that of ἀγχόνη (ankhónē), βελόνη…

3149.t: Formation similar to κληΐς (klēī̈́s) and κνημίς (knēmī́s) which points to a secondary derivative.

3198.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *entós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁éntos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁én. Cognate with Latin intus.

3138.t: The formation is similar to παλάμη (palámē, “palm of the hand”), δόχμη (dókhmē, “breadth of the hand”) and πυγμή (pugmḗ, “distance between the elbow and the knuckles”). According to Beekes, it's probably from Pre-Greek.

3195.t: From ἐν- (en-, “in, into”) + φυσάω (phūsáō, “to blow, to puff”), from φῦσα (phûsă, “pair of bellows”) + -άω (-áō, verbal suffix).

3139.t: The formation is similar to ἀστήρ (ăstḗr, “star”) and αἰθήρ (aithḗr, “ether”).

3194.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁l̥h₂-tós, verbal adjective of *h₁elh₂- (“to drive somewhere”). By surface analysis, ἐλα(ύνω) (ela(únō)) + -τός (-tós).
